newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: IHC Caland upbeat on future prospects.
newsitem.headline: IHC Caland upbeat on future prospects.

text.p: Shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland said on Monday it was extremely upbeat on prospects in its main markets of dredging and offshore supply.
"The markets in which we operate are buzzing with activity and offer a great many opportunities," chairman Jan Bax told a news conference on 1996 first half results.

The main factors driving the offshore supply market were rising demand for oil and gas and higher exploration and production (E/P) budgets. Energy companies' E/P budgets had increased by some 11 percent or more this year, he added.

Never before had there been so many major projects for floating storage and floating production systems (FSO/FPSOs), both for supply and operational lease and IHC Caland was involved in serious discussions on several contracts, he said.
Floating production systems, (in which IHC Caland is world market leader) were becoming more attractive than fixed platforms to oil companies seeking to contain costs, Bax said.
Prospects for the dredging market were also rosy, he added.
"We are very optimistic on the market long term," he said. "There is so much work in the pipeline, particularly in the Far East but also in western Europe."

IHC Caland booked 745 million guilders in new orders in the first half of 1996. This compares with 1.86 billion guilders in new orders for full-1995. The group's order book stood at 3.4 billion guilders at end-June.

"We are very satisfied with incoming orders," Bax said, adding that year-on-year figures were not strictly comparable owing to the "lumpy" (irregular) order intake in the markets where IHC Caland was active.
New orders included the supply and installation of an FPSO for BP's Schiehallion field west of the Shetland Isles.

Unlike previous 'turnkey' projects in which IHC Caland shouldered the full risk, this project will be carried equally by all participants in an alliance comprising IHC Caland's wholly-owned offshore systems subsidiary SBM, Brown & Root, Harland & Wolff and Coflexip/Stena.

IHC Caland said it had also won a 70 million guilder order for the supply of two turret moorings and swivel stacks for two FPSO's to be built by Hyundai Industries for Petrobras of Brazil through the conversion of second-hand tankers.
Bax said IHC kept the construction of turrets and swivel stacks in-house to safeguard its technological advantage.
